key_insight: Ground-state energy accuracy and phonon spectra help predict whether pretrained force fields reproduce zirconia’s monoclinic–tetragonal–cubic phase sequence.
engineering_relevance: These diagnostics offer practical screening criteria for selecting pretrained force fields for lower-cost finite-temperature phase-transition simulations.
method: Benchmark ten open-source universal machine-learning force fields for ZrO₂.
Compare polymorph energetics and phonon dispersions with matched density functional theory references.
Test phase evolution using variable-cell isothermal-isobaric molecular dynamics.
evidence_signal: Four of ten models reproduced the correct phase sequence; orthorhombic–tetragonal energy errors above about 10 meV/atom introduced an orthorhombic intermediate, while ORB-based models showed 30–60% phonon-frequency compression and unstable variable-cell dynamics.
watch_item: The suggested screening criteria—relative polymorph energies within about 6 meV/atom of matched DFT and no systematic phonon softening—are established here for ZrO₂, not validated across materials.
paper_title: Application of Pretrained Universal Machine Learning Force-Fields for Phase Transitions Prediction in ZrO2
